abstract: This paper assesses the network robustness of the technological capability base of 269 European metropolitan areas against the potential elimination of some of their capabilities. By doing so it provides systematic evidence on how network robustness conditioned the economic resilience of these regions in the context of the 2008 economic crisis. The analysis concerns calls in the relevant literature for more in-depth analysis on the link between regional economic network structures and the resilience of regions to economic shocks. By adopting a network science approach that is novel to economic geographic inquiry, the objective is to stress-test the technological resilience of regions by utilizing information on the co-classification of CPC classes listed on European Patent Office patent documents. Findings from a regression analysis indicate that metropolitan regions with a more robust technological knowledge network structure exhibit higher levels of resilience with respect to changes in employment rates. Regions with high levels of employment in industry but with vulnerable technological capability base are particularly challenged by this aspect of regional economic resilience.
summary_en: How does the network structure of regional technological capabilities affect economic resilience to crises? Tóth, Elekes, Whittle, Lee and Kogler analyse 269 European metropolitan areas using EPO patent CPC-class co-classification data, applying network-science 'stress tests' that simulate elimination of technological capabilities. Regions with more robust technological-knowledge network structure showed higher economic resilience (employment-rate stability) during the 2008 crisis, robust to random and targeted elimination strategies. Regions with high industrial employment but fragile technological networks are particularly vulnerable.
data_used: European Patent Office (EPO) patent metadata for ~269 European NUTS-3 metropolitan areas, with CPC-class co-classification networks; regional employment and economic-resilience measures from Eurostat, covering 2007-2014 (the crisis and recovery period).
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for Hungarian regional-development policy and EU Cohesion Fund investments. The paper provides a network-based diagnostic tool for assessing which Hungarian regions have technologically resilient versus fragile capability bases — useful for ITM and Pénzügyminisztérium when allocating regional R&D and innovation funding to maximize crisis resilience.
title: Technology Network Structure Conditions the Economic Resilience of Regions
